name: Orkes: LLM Workflow Uses a Saved Prompt Template by Name (not raw instructions)
query: On our Orkes cluster (auth required; integration openai-prod already has gpt-4o-mini registered) build a workflow that takes a support ticket as input and returns a 3-bullet summary in a friendly tone. Use system instructions telling the model how to summarize.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Recognize Enterprise (auth required) — on Enterprise `instructions` is read as a saved prompt-template name (SKILL.md Rule 18)
Step 2: Write the system prompt to a file with `${...}` placeholders (e.g. `${ticket}`, `${tone}`)
Step 3: Save it as a template associated with the model the task uses: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" prompt-save --name <t> --template-file <f> --model openai-prod:gpt-4o-mini`

Step 4: Write the workflow with LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE: `llmProvider: openai-prod`, `model: gpt-4o-mini`, `instructions: <template name>`, runtime values via `promptVariables` (real expressions like `${workflow.input.ticket}`) and/or the ticket as a user message in `messages`
Step 5: Mention the alternative: literal instructions require `allowRawPrompts: true`
Step 6: Register from a file and verify with a test run
success_criteria: Saves the system prompt as a prompt template (`prompt-save` or `POST /api/prompts/{name}`) rather than putting literal instructions in the task without `allowRawPrompts`
Associates the template with `openai-prod:gpt-4o-mini` (the exact integration:model the task uses)

The task's `instructions` (or `promptName`) is the template name, and runtime data reaches the model through `promptVariables` mapped to real Conductor expressions (e.g. `${workflow.input.ticket}`) and/or a `messages` entry
Does not put template placeholders like `${ticket}` inline in the workflow JSON, where Conductor would treat them as expressions
Mentions that literal prompt text would require `allowRawPrompts: true` on Enterprise
Uses `llmProvider: openai-prod` and `model: gpt-4o-mini`, writes the workflow JSON to a file before registering, and verifies with a run
